props.name: Example III: chromic oxide, nickel oxide and zinc oxide (from nitrates), moistened with zinc chloride

evidence.quote: 4 kilograms chromic nitrate
and 750 grams nickel nitrate
are dissolved in 5 liters of water. 2.5 kilo- grams of zinc oxide is added with stirring and the mass is heated to dryness and is then 15 further heated till no more nitric oxide fumes are given off,
whereby the mixture is transformed to chromic oxide, nickel oxide, . and zinc oxide.
The resultant mass is bro- ‘ken up into granules and is then moistened 20 with a solution containing 450 grams of zinc chloride. The granules are again dried and are ready for use.

props.name: chromic chloride in place of zinc chloride: results not greatly varied

evidence.quote: In place of moistening the sranules of the catalyst in Example III with zinc chloride a chemically equivalent amount of chromic chloride may be employed.
The results will not be greatly varied.

props.statement: Moistening the Example III granules with a chemically equivalent amount of chromic chloride instead of zinc chloride does not greatly vary the results.

props.name: amount of metallic halide

evidence.quote: To produce our improved catalysts it is not necessary that the amount of metallic

halide added bear any exact weight relation to the remaining constituents of the catalyst, though the amount of halide added should preferably be less than one chemical equiva- lent of the amount of principal metallic oxide present in the catalyst.

props.statement: The amount of metallic halide need bear no exact weight relation to the other constituents, but should preferably be less than one chemical equivalent of the amount of principal metallic oxide present.

props.name: halide improves otherwise identical catalysts with copper or silver oxides

evidence.quote: Or we may employ easily reducible oxides such as those of copper or silver which are already known in the art as advantageous compo- nents of certain methanol catalysts.
In these cases however, our improved catalysts containing halides produce far better results than those known in the art for otherwise identical catalyst mixtures.

props.statement: With easily reducible oxides such as those of copper or silver, the improved catalysts containing halides produce far better results than those known in the art for otherwise identical catalyst mixtures.

props.name: halide-containing catalyst gives higher yield of purer methanol and practically no methane

evidence.quote: We have discovered a new type of metha- nol catalyst which produces a higher yield of methanol than those formerly employed in the art, and at the same time produces a 85_ very pure methanol, uncontaminated by by- —
An additional advantage accru-. ing from the use of our catalysts is that the formation of methane in the process—with the consequent destruction of valuable hy- 90 drogen—is practically eliminated.

props.statement: The new type of methanol catalyst produces a higher yield of methanol than those formerly employed, a very pure methanol uncontaminated by by-products, and practically eliminates the formation of methane.

props.name: methanating metals serve advantageously in the halide catalysts

evidence.quote: Tt will be observed that in our-improved catalyst we may employ substances normally deleterious to the methanol reaction— namely the “methanating metals”—iron. 06 — nickel; or vobalt,
compositions these normally deleterious sub- stances serve advantageously, apparently ex- erting only a normal hydrogenating cata- lytic action productive of methanol.

props.statement: In the improved (halide-containing) catalyst compositions the normally deleterious 'methanating metals' iron, nickel or cobalt may be employed and serve advantageously, apparently exerting only a normal hydrogenating catalytic action productive of methanol.

props.name: pure CO gives higher methanol percentage

evidence.quote: Likewise the use of pure carbon monoxide as distinguished from carbon di- oxide or a mixture of the two results in an increased methanol percentage in the con- densate,
since carbon monoxide seems to react more readily, an increased con- densate volume.

props.statement: Pure carbon monoxide, as distinguished from carbon dioxide or a mixture of the two, results in an increased methanol percentage in the condensate and, since carbon monoxide seems to react more readily, an increased condensate volume.
